explain.say: An exoskeleton is a wearable robot: a frame strapped outside the body with motors at the joints. It helps people walk, stand or lift by adding strength where they need it.

faq.q: How does an exoskeleton know what you want to do?
faq.a: Sensors measure joint angles, shifts in weight, foot pressure, and sometimes the electrical signals from muscles. Software recognises patterns, such as leaning forward to start walking, and moves the motors to match.
asks: How do exoskeletons read muscle signals?

faq.q: How does an exoskeleton help you walk?
faq.a: Motors at the hips and knees add turning force at the right moment in each step. Medical exoskeletons let some people with paralysis stand up and walk with crutches.
asks: Can exoskeletons help paralysed people walk?

faq.q: How does an exoskeleton help you lift?
faq.a: It shares the load: springs or motors support the body as you bend and lift, and the rigid frame carries part of the weight to the ground, reducing strain on the back and shoulders.
asks: How do exoskeletons help workers lift?

faq.a: No. Passive exoskeletons use springs or elastic bands that store energy when you bend and give it back when you straighten, helping with overhead work or lifting without any battery.
Medical walking exoskeletons often weigh around 20 to 25 kilograms, but the frame carries its own weight down to the ground, so the wearer does not feel all of it.

facts: In 2014 the ReWalk became the first powered exoskeleton cleared by the US FDA for personal use by people with spinal cord injuries.
Passive exoskeletons use springs instead of motors and need no battery.

quiz.say: What does a passive exoskeleton use instead of motors?
quiz.why: Springs store energy when you bend and give it back as you straighten, with no motor or battery.

wrong.1: Jet engines are not used in wearable exoskeletons.
wrong.2: A passive exoskeleton has no engine or pump at all.
